newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's March industrial production up 4.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's March industrial production up 4.2 pct.

text.p: Mexico's industrial production grew 4.2 percent during March compared to the same month a year ago, the Finance Ministry said on Wednesday.
A Reuters survey of 10 brokerages, banks and research firms in Mexico City had forecast industrial activity growth of 7.65 percent during March.
The ministry added that industrial production would have been 11 percent had there not been fewer working days during the month due to the Easter Holy Week.
During the year's first quarter, industrial production rose 6.2 percent, compared to the same period of 1996.
Mining production rose 1.0 percent from January to March compared to the same period a year earlier.
Mining production excluding petroleum rose 1.6 percent in the first three months of the year, while petroleum production rose 2.9 percent, the Ministry said.

Manufacturing grew 6.2 percent during the quarter compared to the first three months of 1996. Output in the maquiladora, or in-bond, industry rose 14.2 percent while production in the non-maquila manufacturing sector rose 5.7 percent.

Construction rose 8.7 percent in real terms in the first three months, the fourth consecutive quarter of growth in that sector. Generation of electricity, gas and water grew 5.1 percent during the quarter.

During the month of March alone, mining output grew 0.5 percent compared the same month of 1996. Manufacturing grew 3.7 percent, construction grew 7.5 percent, and electricity, gas and water rose 5.1 percent.
Holy Week took place in April of 1996 and in March of this year, meaning there were three fewer working days during March than during the same month of 1996, the ministry said.
